label: CNV
text: Choroidal neovascularization (CNV) refers to the growth of new, abnormal blood vessels from the choroid through Bruch's membrane into the sub-retinal pigment epithelial or subretinal space.

label: CNV
text: On OCT, CNV typically presents as a hyperreflective irregular lesion beneath the RPE, often associated with subretinal fluid and disruption of the ellipsoid zone.

label: CNV
text: Subretinal fluid appearing as a hyporeflective space between the neurosensory retina and RPE is a hallmark of active CNV.

label: CNV
text: Type 1 CNV (occult) grows beneath the RPE, producing a pigment epithelial detachment visible as a dome-shaped elevation of the RPE on OCT.

label: CNV
text: Type 2 CNV (classic) grows through the RPE into the subretinal space, appearing as a hyperreflective lesion above the RPE layer.

label: CNV
text: Type 3 CNV, also called retinal angiomatous proliferation, originates from the deep retinal capillary plexus and grows downward toward the RPE.

label: CNV
text: Intraretinal fluid cysts in combination with sub-RPE material strongly suggest neovascular AMD with active CNV.

label: CNV
text: Anti-VEGF therapy is the standard of care for CNV, targeting vascular endothelial growth factor to suppress new vessel growth and reduce exudation.

label: CNV
text: Irregular RPE elevation with overlying intraretinal or subretinal fluid on OCT is highly suggestive of CNV requiring prompt treatment.

label: CNV
text: A fibrovascular pigment epithelial detachment shows a shallow, irregular RPE elevation with heterogeneous internal reflectivity, distinguishing it from a serous PED.

label: CNV
text: Subretinal hyperreflective material on OCT represents fibrin, blood, or fibrosis associated with active or healing CNV lesions.

label: CNV
text: Polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy, a CNV variant, shows notched or multilobular PEDs on OCT corresponding to polypoidal lesions on indocyanine green angiography.

label: CNV
text: Persistent subretinal fluid despite anti-VEGF therapy may indicate treatment-resistant CNV or a tachyphylaxis response requiring switch in agent.

label: CNV
text: Disruption of the external limiting membrane and ellipsoid zone overlying a CNV lesion correlates with poorer visual prognosis even after fluid resolution.

label: CNV
text: Subretinal fluid in CNV is typically optically clear and located between the photoreceptor outer segments and the RPE, distinct from intraretinal cystic fluid.

label: CNV
text: A flat irregular PED with shaggy or undulating contour on OCT is a classic sign of CNV rather than simple drusenoid PED.

label: CNV
text: Double-layer sign on OCT, where a shallow irregular RPE elevation parallels a hyperreflective band, suggests a non-exudative or quiescent CNV.

label: CNV
text: Hemorrhagic PED appears as a dome-shaped RPE elevation with markedly hyperreflective, dense internal contents obscuring underlying choroidal detail.

label: CNV
text: Loss of the normal foveal contour combined with cystic intraretinal fluid and subretinal fluid indicates significant exudative activity from CNV.

label: CNV
text: Treat-and-extend regimens for CNV use OCT-detected fluid as the primary biomarker to titrate the interval between anti-VEGF injections.

label: CNV
text: Myopic CNV occurs in highly myopic eyes and appears as a small, dome-shaped hyperreflective subretinal lesion, often without significant fluid.

label: CNV
text: Idiopathic CNV in younger patients without drusen or AMD risk factors may present similarly to AMD-related CNV but typically responds well to limited anti-VEGF treatment.

label: CNV
text: Recurrent CNV activity after a quiescent period often manifests first as new intraretinal cystic fluid on OCT before subjective vision changes occur.

label: CNV
text: A notched or peaked PED contour on OCT, sometimes called the thumb sign, can indicate an underlying polypoidal lesion in polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy.

label: CNV
text: Pachychoroid neovasculopathy is a CNV subtype associated with thickened choroid and dilated Haller layer vessels, often without typical drusen.

label: CNV
text: Quantification of subretinal and intraretinal fluid volume on OCT is used in clinical trials as a continuous outcome measure for anti-VEGF efficacy in CNV.

label: CNV
text: Active CNV lesions often show intraretinal hyperreflective dots adjacent to the area of subretinal fluid, representing migrating inflammatory or RPE cells.

label: CNV
text: Macular atrophy can develop as a late complication of chronic or recurrent CNV, appearing on OCT as thinning and hypertransmission through the outer retina and RPE.

label: CNV
text: Subfoveal CNV carries a worse visual prognosis than extrafoveal CNV due to direct involvement of the photoreceptor layer responsible for central vision.

label: CNV
text: A shallow irregular RPE elevation overlying a markedly thickened choroid, without classic drusen, suggests pachychoroid-associated CNV rather than typical AMD-related CNV.

label: CNV
text: OCT angiography can directly visualize the abnormal neovascular network within a CNV lesion without requiring dye-based angiography.

label: CNV
text: Vitreous hemorrhage may rarely complicate aggressive CNV lesions, appearing as diffuse hyperreflective material obscuring the view of underlying retinal structures on OCT.

label: CNV
text: Combination therapy with anti-VEGF and photodynamic therapy is sometimes used for polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy lesions resistant to anti-VEGF monotherapy.

label: CNV
text: Geographic atrophy can coexist with treated CNV, appearing on OCT as sharply demarcated areas of outer retinal and RPE loss adjacent to the fibrotic neovascular scar.

label: CNV
text: A disciform scar represents the end-stage fibrotic outcome of chronic CNV, appearing on OCT as a dense, organized hyperreflective subretinal mass without active fluid.

label: DME
text: Diabetic macular edema (DME) is characterized by intraretinal fluid accumulation in the macula secondary to breakdown of the inner blood-retinal barrier.

label: DME
text: OCT in DME shows retinal thickening with hyporeflective intraretinal cystic spaces, most prominent in the outer plexiform and inner nuclear layers.

label: DME
text: Center-involved DME refers to edema affecting the central 1mm subfield of the macula, which is the primary target for treatment decisions.

label: DME
text: Hard exudates appear as discrete hyperreflective foci with posterior shadowing on OCT and indicate lipid deposition from chronic vascular leakage in DME.

label: DME
text: Diffuse retinal thickening without distinct cysts, sometimes described as sponge-like swelling, is a common OCT pattern in early or mild DME.

label: DME
text: Vitreomacular traction may exacerbate DME, with OCT showing posterior hyaloid attachment and tractional elevation of the retinal surface.

label: DME
text: Anti-VEGF injections and corticosteroid implants are first-line treatments for center-involving DME associated with vision loss.

label: DME
text: Ellipsoid zone disruption in DME on OCT correlates with photoreceptor damage and predicts worse visual acuity outcomes after treatment.

label: DME
text: Cystoid macular edema in DME produces large, well-demarcated hyporeflective cystic spaces predominantly in the inner nuclear and outer plexiform layers.

label: DME
text: Subretinal fluid can also accompany DME in more severe cases, appearing as a hyporeflective space beneath the neurosensory retina without RPE elevation.

label: DME
text: Disorganization of the retinal inner layers, where boundaries between ganglion cell, inner plexiform, and inner nuclear layers become indistinct, predicts poor visual recovery in chronic DME.

label: DME
text: Central subfield thickness measured by OCT is the standard quantitative metric used to track DME severity and treatment response over time.

label: DME
text: Microaneurysms appear on OCT as small round hyperreflective structures, often located adjacent to areas of intraretinal cystic fluid in DME.

label: DME
text: Epiretinal membrane formation can coexist with DME, appearing as a thin hyperreflective line on the retinal surface that may contribute to tractional edema.

label: DME
text: Severe non-proliferative or proliferative diabetic retinopathy with DME may show OCT evidence of preretinal hemorrhage or fibrovascular proliferation at the vitreoretinal interface.

label: DME
text: Resolution of intraretinal cysts on OCT following anti-VEGF therapy is the primary structural endpoint used to gauge treatment response in DME trials.

label: DME
text: Focal laser photocoagulation is reserved for non-center-involving DME with focal leakage points identified on fluorescein angiography, correlated with OCT thickening.

label: DME
text: Large cystoid spaces spanning the full retinal thickness, sometimes with bridging septae, indicate chronic and severe DME with guarded visual prognosis.

label: DME
text: Foveal bulge or loss of the normal foveal depression on OCT indicates significant central edema even before symptomatic vision loss in DME.

label: DME
text: Intravitreal corticosteroid implants such as dexamethasone are particularly effective for DME with a significant inflammatory component evidenced by hyperreflective foci.

label: DME
text: Hyperreflective foci scattered within the retinal layers on OCT in DME are thought to represent activated microglia or lipid-laden macrophages indicating inflammation.

label: DME
text: Serous retinal detachment in DME is distinguished from CNV-related subretinal fluid by the absence of any associated RPE elevation or sub-RPE material.

label: DME
text: Outer retinal layer disruption combined with large cystic spaces on OCT in DME is associated with reduced likelihood of visual acuity improvement despite anatomic resolution.

label: DME
text: Recurrent DME after treatment discontinuation typically reappears first as subtle outer plexiform layer thickening before progressing to visible cysts.

label: DME
text: Diabetic papillopathy, occasionally associated with severe DME, can show optic disc edema on OCT in addition to macular thickening.

label: DME
text: Macular ischemia, identified by enlargement of the foveal avascular zone, frequently coexists with DME and limits the visual benefit achievable from edema resolution alone.

label: DME
text: Intraretinal cysts in early DME are often small and confined to a single layer, while advanced DME shows multilayer cystic involvement spanning the full retinal thickness.

label: DME
text: Pseudophakic cystoid macular edema can mimic DME on OCT but typically arises following cataract surgery and has a different underlying inflammatory mechanism.

label: DME
text: Combination anti-VEGF and steroid therapy may be considered for DME eyes with mixed vascular and inflammatory components evident on OCT.

label: DME
text: Photoreceptor outer segment length, measured between the ellipsoid zone and the RPE on OCT, is reduced in eyes with chronic DME and correlates with visual function.

label: DME
text: Spontaneous resolution of mild DME can occur in a subset of patients with well-controlled systemic glycemia, observable as gradual thinning on serial OCT scans.

label: DRUSEN
text: Drusen are extracellular deposits beneath the retinal pigment epithelium, composed of lipids, proteins, and cellular debris, and are the hallmark of early and intermediate age-related macular degeneration.

label: DRUSEN
text: On OCT, soft drusen appear as dome-shaped, medium-reflective elevations of the RPE with a distinct base and apex, without overlying retinal fluid.

label: DRUSEN
text: Hard drusen are small, discrete, and hyperreflective on OCT; they carry low risk of progression to advanced AMD compared to soft or confluent drusen.

label: DRUSEN
text: Drusen volume and area measured on OCT are quantitative biomarkers used to stratify the risk of progression from intermediate to late AMD.

label: DRUSEN
text: Subretinal drusenoid deposits, also called reticular pseudodrusen, appear as hyperreflective material above the RPE rather than beneath it, and are associated with increased AMD progression risk.

label: DRUSEN
text: Drusen regression, defined as a reduction in drusen volume over time, paradoxically precedes RPE atrophy in advanced dry AMD rather than indicating improvement.

label: DRUSEN
text: The presence of large soft drusen exceeding 125 micrometers in diameter, combined with pigmentary changes, substantially increases the 5-year risk of progression to neovascular or atrophic AMD.

label: DRUSEN
text: Outer retinal tubulations adjacent to drusen on OCT indicate photoreceptor degeneration and emerging RPE atrophy in geographic atrophy.

label: DRUSEN
text: Confluent drusen, where multiple individual deposits merge into a continuous undulating elevation of the RPE, indicate more advanced intermediate AMD with higher progression risk.

label: DRUSEN
text: Hyporeflective cores within drusen on OCT, sometimes called drusen cores, are associated with increased likelihood of progression to geographic atrophy.

label: DRUSEN
text: Calcified drusen appear as highly hyperreflective, well-demarcated deposits with posterior shadowing and are a risk factor for impending RPE atrophy.

label: DRUSEN
text: Cuticular drusen, a distinct subtype occurring in younger patients, appear as numerous small, uniform, dome-shaped elevations producing a characteristic starry sky pattern on OCT en face imaging.

label: DRUSEN
text: Pigment epithelial detachments composed primarily of drusenoid material show a homogeneous medium-reflective internal signal, distinguishing them from the heterogeneous signal of a fibrovascular PED.

label: DRUSEN
text: Hyperreflective foci overlying drusen on OCT represent migrating RPE cells and are an early biomarker for impending atrophy in that location.

label: DRUSEN
text: AREDS2 formulation supplements containing antioxidants, zinc, and lutein/zeaxanthin are recommended for patients with intermediate AMD and large drusen to slow progression.

label: DRUSEN
text: Drusenoid pigment epithelial detachment is defined on OCT as a broad, shallow RPE elevation greater than 350 micrometers wide caused by confluent drusen material.

label: DRUSEN
text: Loss of the RPE band integrity overlying a drusenoid PED, combined with adjacent photoreceptor loss, indicates early transition toward geographic atrophy.

label: DRUSEN
text: Drusen are typically bilateral and symmetric in distribution, which helps distinguish age-related drusen from unilateral pseudodrusen patterns seen in other conditions.

label: DRUSEN
text: Basal laminar drusen, a variant seen in younger patients, show as small uniform sawtooth-pattern elevations of the RPE on OCT cross-section.

label: DRUSEN
text: Choroidal thinning beneath areas of extensive drusen on OCT may be an early structural change preceding clinically visible geographic atrophy.

label: DRUSEN
text: The absence of intraretinal or subretinal fluid is a key OCT feature distinguishing simple drusen from drusen complicated by early exudative CNV.

label: DRUSEN
text: Nascent geographic atrophy, an OCT-defined precursor lesion, shows subsidence of the outer plexiform and inner nuclear layers overlying drusen with hyporeflective wedge-shaped changes.

label: DRUSEN
text: Reticular pseudodrusen are best visualized on near-infrared reflectance imaging as a network of interlacing ribbon-like lesions, corresponding to discrete hyperreflective deposits above the RPE on OCT cross-section.

label: DRUSEN
text: Drusen distribution patterns differ by location: macular drusen confer higher AMD progression risk than peripheral drusen, which are more often age-related without pathologic significance.

label: DRUSEN
text: Complete RPE and outer retinal atrophy, the OCT-defined endpoint of geographic atrophy, shows increased signal hypertransmission into the choroid due to loss of the overlying RPE.

label: DRUSEN
text: Incomplete RPE and outer retinal atrophy represents an intermediate OCT stage between intact drusen and complete atrophy, characterized by partial RPE attenuation without frank hypertransmission.

label: DRUSEN
text: Multiple coalescing drusen with overlying photoreceptor disruption but without fluid should prompt close monitoring for early conversion to either atrophic or neovascular AMD.

label: NORMAL
text: A normal OCT macula shows a smooth foveal contour with a central pit, distinct retinal layers, an intact ellipsoid zone, and no fluid or drusen.

label: NORMAL
text: The normal foveal avascular zone appears as a central depression on OCT with thinning of the inner retinal layers and preservation of the outer retinal bands.

label: NORMAL
text: In a healthy retina, the RPE and Bruch's membrane complex appears as a continuous, uniformly hyperreflective band without elevations or disruptions.

label: NORMAL
text: Normal central subfield thickness on OCT is approximately 250 to 270 micrometers in women and 270 to 290 micrometers in men on spectral-domain OCT.

label: NORMAL
text: The ellipsoid zone, previously called the inner segment/outer segment junction, appears as a bright, continuous hyperreflective line in the normal outer retina.

label: NORMAL
text: Normal OCT shows no intraretinal cysts, no subretinal fluid, no RPE elevations, and no hyperreflective foci indicative of pathology.

label: NORMAL
text: The inner segment/outer segment junction and the cone outer segment tip line are both visible and intact in a normal healthy macula.

label: NORMAL
text: Age-related thinning of the retinal nerve fiber layer on OCT is a normal physiologic finding and should be distinguished from pathologic glaucomatous loss.

label: NORMAL
text: A normal foveal contour displays a gradual, symmetric depression without abrupt elevations, irregularities, or flattening of the central pit.

label: NORMAL
text: The external limiting membrane appears as a thin, continuous hyperreflective line just above the ellipsoid zone in a structurally normal retina.

label: NORMAL
text: Normal choroidal thickness varies by age and axial length but typically ranges from 250 to 350 micrometers in the subfoveal region in healthy adults.

label: NORMAL
text: The posterior vitreous in a normal young eye remains attached to the retinal surface without evidence of traction, detachment, or epiretinal membrane formation.

label: NORMAL
text: All nine standard retinal layers, from the nerve fiber layer to the RPE, are clearly delineated and uniformly reflective in a normal OCT scan.

label: NORMAL
text: No pigment epithelial detachment, drusen, or sub-RPE deposits are present in a structurally and functionally normal macula on OCT.

label: NORMAL
text: A normal OCT angiogram, when available, shows an intact and regular foveal avascular zone without areas of capillary nonperfusion or neovascular flow.

label: NORMAL
text: Symmetric retinal thickness between the two eyes, in the absence of high refractive error or prior pathology, is expected in a normal OCT examination.

label: NORMAL
text: The optic nerve head and peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness fall within established normative age-adjusted ranges in a healthy eye.

label: NORMAL
text: Mild physiologic cupping of the optic disc on OCT, without focal notching or progressive nerve fiber layer thinning, is a normal anatomic variant.

label: NORMAL
text: A normal vitreomacular interface shows no adhesion, traction, or membrane formation, with a clear separation between the posterior hyaloid and the internal limiting membrane.

label: NORMAL
text: Normal photoreceptor outer segment length is consistent across the macula in a healthy eye, without focal shortening or disruption near the fovea.

label: NORMAL
text: In emmetropic or mildly ametropic normal eyes, the retinal layers maintain consistent thickness and reflectivity from the fovea to the perifoveal region.

label: NORMAL
text: A normal scan shows uniform choroidal reflectivity without focal thinning, thickening, or the dilated outer choroidal vessels seen in pachychoroid spectrum disease.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Unlike DME, subretinal fluid in CNV originates beneath the RPE rather than within retinal layers, and is not typically associated with diabetic vascular changes.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Unlike CNV, intraretinal cysts in DME are distributed across multiple retinal layers and correlate with vascular leakage seen on fluorescein angiography in diabetic patients.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Unlike CNV, simple drusen do not produce overlying intraretinal or subretinal fluid unless neovascularization has developed secondarily.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Unlike DME cystic spaces, drusen are located beneath the RPE and do not cause thickening or cystic change above the RPE layer.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Distinguishing CNV from drusen on OCT: CNV produces subretinal fluid and an irregular RPE elevation, whereas drusen cause smooth, regular RPE undulations without fluid.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: A serous PED from CNV typically shows a smooth dome-shaped elevation with optically empty internal reflectivity, whereas a drusenoid PED shows medium internal reflectivity from solid material.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: DME cysts are typically round and well-circumscribed within retinal layers, while CNV-associated subretinal fluid is a flatter, more diffuse space beneath the photoreceptors.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Normal age-related foveal thinning should not be confused with pathologic atrophy; the former preserves all retinal layers while the latter shows loss of the RPE and photoreceptor bands.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Vitreomacular traction can mimic DME by causing retinal thickening, but is distinguished by visible posterior hyaloid attachment and the absence of true intraretinal cystic fluid.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Pseudodrusen differ from conventional drusen in that they are located above the RPE rather than beneath it, appearing as a hyperreflective layer overlying an otherwise intact RPE band.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: CNV occurring in a previously drusen-laden eye should be suspected when new intraretinal or subretinal fluid appears adjacent to pre-existing drusen on follow-up OCT.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Diabetic patients with concurrent AMD may show both DME-pattern intraretinal cysts and drusen on the same OCT scan, requiring careful layer-by-layer differentiation of each finding.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Cystoid macular edema can arise from DME, CNV, or postsurgical inflammation; the surrounding OCT context, such as presence of drusen or diabetic microaneurysms, helps distinguish the underlying cause.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: A normal scan and an early drusen-only scan can appear similar at low magnification; the key distinguishing feature is any RPE elevation, however subtle, which is absent in a truly normal macula.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Subretinal hyperreflective material is seen in active CNV but not in uncomplicated DME or simple drusen, making it a useful discriminating feature on OCT.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Hard exudates in DME are hyperreflective with posterior shadowing similar to calcified drusen, but their distribution within retinal layers rather than beneath the RPE distinguishes the two.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Geographic atrophy from advanced dry AMD and outer retinal atrophy from chronic resolved DME can both show hypertransmission on OCT, but differ in the pattern of antecedent findings such as drusen versus diabetic microvascular changes.

label: DIFFERENTIAL
text: Disorganization of retinal inner layers is a feature specific to chronic DME and is not typically seen in CNV or drusen-only eyes, helping localize chronicity of diabetic disease.
